svg.title: FlashAttention-4 backward · SM100 role, synchronization, and memory timeline
svg.desc: A three-phase reconstruction of the dense head-dimension-128 one-CTA FlashAttentionBackwardSm100 path. Load warp 13 stages fixed K and V plus streamed Q, dO, LSE, and D. MMA warp 12 owns tensor memory and issues S, dP, dV, dQ, and dK. Compute warps reconstruct P and dS, reduce warps drain dQ, and the epilogue reuses operand shared memory for dK and dV staging. Tensor-memory sequential aliases are aligned to the same semantic event axis.
svg.text: FlashAttention-4 backward · SM100 dense D=128, one CTA
Fixed K/V serve one n-block while Qⱼ, dOⱼ, saved LSEⱼ, and Dⱼ stream across the row loop. Widths show semantic order, not cycles.
Selected path: tile M×N=128×128 · Q stages=2 · dO stages=1 · no 2-CTA relay · nondeterministic dQ reduce-add.
reconstruct P and dS from TMEM
Compute barriers make the S→P and dP→dS/dQ overwrites legal only after every reader finishes.
same allocation sized to later stage sdK
same allocation sized to later stage sdV
TMEM S→P and dP→dS→dQ are sequential aliases, not simultaneous tiles
sQ → sdK and sdO → sdV after their final operand consumers
Dⱼ denotes dPsum / rowsum(dOⱼ ⊙ Oⱼ), produced by the preprocessing kernel and consumed with saved LSEⱼ.
MEMORY LIFETIMES · SAME PROLOGUE / MAINLOOP / EPILOGUE AXIS

g.text: sQ₀ / sQⱼ ring · live until final dK issue
sdOⱼ · live until final dP/dV issue
dK and dV accumulate across Qⱼ rows, then drain in epilogue

svg.text: Bars share the role timeline's phase boundaries; small gaps mark required barriers before physical bytes change identity.
